rows.grounds: sparśa in nominative singular masculine; names the touch element
compound of marut (wind), sva (own/self), and sahita (united/associated); nominative singular masculine agreeing with sparśa
compound of hṛd (heart), dāhena (by burning), ambu (water), and saṃyutam (united); accusative/neuter singular agreeing with the pervaded triad or element

items.question: How is the touch element united with wind and water in this tantric elemental mapping?
premises: touch is united with one's own wind
touch is united with water through heart-burning
items.inference: The verse maps touch to wind through self-association and to water through heart-burning, continuing the elemental correspondence sequence.
uncertainties: exact syntactic relation of hṛddāhenāmbusaṃyutam to sparśo versus the pervaded triad
whether marutsva means one's own wind or wind itself
items.plain_english: Touch is united with its own wind and with water through heart-burning.
